result.title: Represented but Not Used: Value-Policy Dissociation in LLM Agents
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents need to choose actions whose consequences unfold over multiple future steps, yet poor decisions do not reveal whether the model failed to represent those consequences or failed to use them. Mechanistic interpretability has studied internal representations of environment state and plans, but sequential decision making also requires evaluating how candidate actions change future outcomes. Reinforcement learning formalizes this as action value. We study this computation in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, and GPT-OSS-20B across a partially observed Grid environment and WebShop, a simulated web shopping environment. We find that the relative values of candidate actions are linearly decodable from intermediate hidden states, including at states where the policy prefers a worse action. We call this gap between value representation and policy choice value-policy dissociation. To investigate how represented value relates to action selection, we compare direct interventions along the value readout direction with Natural Value Transport (NVT), a transformation learned from hidden state changes that naturally result from differences in action value. While readout-direction interventions have limited and inconsistent effects, NVT more consistently influences action preferences, particularly at later layers. We also test a closed-loop controller that uses the value readout as a sensor and NVT as an actuator, observing improvements in task outcomes. These results suggest that LLM agents can represent useful prospective value without reliably translating it into policy choice.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 Grid 与 WebShop 环境中研究 LLM 智能体的动作价值能否从隐藏状态线性解码，并比较价值读出方向干预与自然价值迁移（NVT）对策略选择的因果影响，提出价值表示与策略选择之间的「价值—策略分离」，并测试以价值读出为传感器、NVT 为执行器的闭环控制器。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽不涉及视觉推理，但其「可解码却未被策略使用」的诊断及基于自然状态变化的干预方法，可能为核查 LVR 中 latent 内容是否真正参与答案生成、区分表示与使用及贡献分配提供可借鉴线索。
